deviations.what: The bootstrap recipe was not followed literally. The command says to commit, replace the placeholder with the new commit's short sha, and amend before pushing. That was done and then undone, because it does not produce what the command requires: a commit cannot contain its own sha, so the amend discards the very commit the stamp names. The stamp resolved locally only because the pre-amend object had not yet been collected; after a push and merge it would not have been an ancestor of main. Instead the restoration is commit 4bfbbc5 and a second commit f5b5810 carries only the stamp lines naming it.
deviations.why: The command's real requirement is stated in its own constraint — that every 'as of <sha>' stamp resolve, and in the merge-commit constraint, that the stamps stay resolvable ancestors of main. Two commits is the only arrangement that satisfies both. This is instrument repair: it changes how reliably the stamp means what it claims, not what the document concludes.
deviations.impact: Two commits on the branch instead of one. The diff against b4e1b9b is unaffected.

deviations.what: The §3.1 prose about shared loop bodies was rewritten rather than only extended with the two new rows.
deviations.why: The restored sentence read: 'recovery_loop and review_rework_loop run the identical eight-node body — the build body plus rework_review and review_fold'. Adding blocked_check and blocked_gate to build_loop makes that sentence false, because the build body is now eight nodes of its own and the shared body is a different eight. Leaving it would have restored a claim that the YAML contradicts, which is the exact class of defect the guards exist to prevent. The replacement states what yaml.safe_load returns and nothing more.

questions_for_advisor: A FINDING THAT NEEDS A RULING. Writing the two new nodes into §3.1 made an asymmetry visible that the YAML has carried since aac0324 and no document stated. build_loop's body is [implement, blocked_check, blocked_gate, domain_review, coverage, consistency, validate, judges]. recovery_loop's and review_rework_loop's shared body is [implement, domain_review, coverage, consistency, validate, judges, rework_review, review_fold] — no blocked_check, no blocked_gate. The honest-refusal gate therefore watches the first build and not the rework or recovery passes, so an implementation that becomes blocked on a criterion after a review sends it back reaches no gate that can report it. That is loop wiring and on the advisor's side of the boundary, so it is recorded in §3.1 and flagged here, and nothing in workflows/engineering-rnd.yaml was touched. Blueprint 016 is exactly the arc in which a ruling on it belongs.

The evidence on the command's own open question — was the truncation deliberate? — points one way. All five guard failures were of the class 'the claim is absent', none 'the number is wrong'. A deliberate slimming would have carried the guard edits that make the slimmed document legal; the guards were untouched, and the document was left in a state where its own test suite fails. Combined with the silent commit message and the hand-typed placeholder sha, the restoration reading is the supported one. The owner still owns the answer.

Deferred to the advisor as the command directs: §4.2's B13 row is unannotated, and §4.1's blueprint counts are unchanged, even though 016's verify_grounding override and blocked_on gate have landed in the graph. Both are record rulings and ride separately.

Not covered by any command in this set: Blueprint 016 was never pasted into docs/handover-review.md as §27, though three of its commits have landed and docs/preregistration-b016-part-e.md cites '§27 (the blueprint, committed before execution)'. The notebook stops at §26. The protocol's paste-before-executing rule was not followed for 016.
